title: Thin lenses and image formation
subtitle: Focusing light rays to construct real and virtual images

learn.prompt: A converging lens has a focal length of 10 cm. An illuminated object sits 30 cm in front of the lens. Adjust the sensor position (image distance di) to capture a focused real image.
learn.explanation: Solving 1/di = 1/10 - 1/30 gives di = 15 cm. Light rays converging past the lens meet in focus at 15 cm on the opposite side.

learn.prompt: An object is placed exactly at distance do = 2f from a converging lens. Where does the focused image form?
learn.explanation: 1/di = 1/f - 1/(2f) = 1/(2f), so di = 2f. The image forms at 2f with an exact 1:1 magnification.

options.label: At the focal point di = f

misconceptionMap.b: An image only forms at f when the incoming light arrives from infinity (parallel rays).
misconceptionMap.c: An image forms at infinity when the object sits directly at the focal point (do = f).
misconceptionMap.d: The thin lens equation yields di = 2f, not 4f.

check.prompt: A camera lens has a focal length of 12 cm. An object stands at do = 24 cm. Where must the film or sensor be placed behind the lens?
check.explanation: Because do = 2f (24 = 2 x 12), the image forms at exactly di = 24 cm.

check.prompt: When an object is placed inside the focal length (do < f) of a magnifying lens, what kind of image is produced?
check.hint: The rays diverge after exiting the lens, appearing to originate from behind the object.
check.explanation: When do < f, 1/di is negative, meaning the image is virtual, upright, and magnified (like looking through a magnifying glass).

options.label: A real, upright image on the other side

misconceptionMap.b: A real inverted image only forms when the object is outside the focal point (do > f).
misconceptionMap.c: Rays refract through the lens, but they diverge rather than converge.
misconceptionMap.d: A real image produced by a single lens is always inverted.

takeaway.title: The thin lens equation connects focal length and image position
takeaway.body: The relationship 1/f = 1/do + 1/di determines where rays converge. For objects beyond the focal point (do > f), a real inverted image forms. For objects closer than the focal point (do < f), diverging rays appear to form a virtual, upright image.
